t: Syria seceded from the United Arab Republic on 28 September 1961; the Ba'athist coup of 8 March 1963 then founded a one-party state that ruled under martial law until 2011 and fell in December 2024.

Hafez al-Assad's Corrective Movement of November 1970 made the Ba'athist state a hereditary dictatorship: Alawite loyalists held the key posts, a cult of personality surrounded the family, and his son Bashar succeeded him in 2000.

The uprising that began on 26 January 2011 became a thirteen-year civil war with more than 600,000 dead, over 5 million refugees and a GDP that shrank by 84% between 2010 and 2023; Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham took Damascus on 8 December 2024.
dyk: By 2021 the amphetamine captagon, produced by associates and relatives of Bashar al-Assad, was Syria's largest export at a minimum of US$3.4 billion a year, against about US$122 million for olive oil, its largest legal export.
ev: On 28 September a coup takes Syria out of the United Arab Republic and ends the political union with Egypt.
On 8 March the Military Committee of the Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party seizes power and establishes a one-party state under martial law.
In the Six-Day War Israel captures two-thirds of the Golan Heights in under 48 hours.
Hafez al-Assad, Minister of Defense, deposes Salah Jadid in the bloodless Corrective Movement and becomes the state's strongman.
The Islamist uprising of the Muslim Brotherhood ends in the Hama massacre, in which Ba'athist troops and paramilitaries kill between 2,000 and 40,000 people.
Hafez al-Assad dies on 10 June; his son Bashar is elected president unopposed, and the Damascus Spring is suppressed by autumn 2001.
Protests from 26 January become a nationwide uprising; the army is sent against the cities and defectors form the Free Syrian Army.
On 8 December opposition forces led by Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham capture Damascus, ending 53 years of Assad family rule; Bashar al-Assad flees to Moscow.

f.predecessor: The United Arab Republic (1958–1961), and before it the Syrian Republic independent of the French Mandate (1946)
